import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Inverse Galois problem

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_Galois_problem)
-/

namespace InverseGalois

structure GaloisRealization.{u, v} (K : Type u) (G : Type v) [Field K] [Group G] where
  -- Every Galois extension of `K : Type u` injects into `AlgebraicClosure K : Type u`.
  -- We therefore lose no generality assuming `L : Type u`.
  L : Type u
  to_field : Field L
  to_algebra : Algebra K L
  to_isGalois : IsGalois K L
  iso : G ≃* (L ≃ₐ[K] L)

/--
Say a group `G` is realizable over a field `K` if it
is isomorphic to the Galois group of a Galois extension
of `K`
-/
class IsRealizable (K G : Type*) [Field K] [Group G] where
  exists_realization : Nonempty (GaloisRealization K G)

/--
The **Inverse Galois Problem**: every finite group is
isomorphic to the Galois group of a Galois extension of the
rationals.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G] :
    IsRealizable ℚ G := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite cyclic group is realizable.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.cyclic
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G] [IsCyclic G] :
    IsRealizable ℚ G := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite abelian group is realizable.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.abelian
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [CommGroup G] :
    IsRealizable ℚ G := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite symmetric group is realizable.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.symmetric_group
    {S : Type*} [Fintype S] :
    IsRealizable ℚ (S ≃ S) := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite group is realisable over the field of rational functions
with complex coefficients.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.complex_rational_functions
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G] :
    IsRealizable (RatFunc ℂ) G := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite group is realisable over the field of rational functions
with coefficients `K`, where `K` is any field of characteristic 0.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.complex_function_field
    {G K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] [Fintype G] [Group G] :
    IsRealizable (RatFunc K) G := by
  sorry

end InverseGalois

findings.description: The coefficient field K is assumed only to satisfy [Field K] [CharZero K] (line 97), but the cited solved result also requires K to be algebraically closed. This is a substantive overgeneralization: taking K := ℚ is accepted by Lean and asserts that every finite group is realizable over ℚ(t). Hilbert irreducibility would then give realizations over ℚ, settling the main inverse Galois problem. Thus this is not merely an outdated status tag. The docstring repeats the missing hypothesis.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, “Inverse Galois problem,” §Partial results (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_Galois_problem#Partial_results), states realizability over “function fields in one variable over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.” Jensen–Ledet–Yui, Generic Polynomials (2002), Introduction, pp. 2–3, confirms the algebraically closed coefficient-field result and explains that a Galois extension of ℚ(t), “regular or not,” specializes to an extension of ℚ with the same Galois group: https://library.slmath.org/books/Book45/files/book45start.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Add [IsAlgClosed K] to the hypotheses: `{G K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K] [Fintype G] [Group G] : IsRealizable (RatFunc K) G`. Update the docstring to say that K is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. The research solved category is appropriate for this corrected statement.

reformulations.difference: The realization is packaged in a structure whose extension field lives in the base field’s universe, and finite degree is left implicit rather than required by a separate FiniteDimensional field.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite G, the group isomorphism makes the Galois group finite, so IsGalois.finiteDimensional_of_finite proves that the extension has finite degree. Conversely, an explicitly finite Galois realization supplies the structure. The universe restriction also loses nothing: any Galois extension is algebraic and embeds into AlgebraicClosure K; its image is a same-universe K-isomorphic extension, with isomorphic automorphism group by conjugation. ULift transports witnesses in the other direction. The scratch theorem Review.realizable_iff_wide_finite proves the full equivalence with existence of an explicitly finite Galois extension in Type (max u w).

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_Galois_problem — entire article, including partial results, cyclic/abelian constructions, symmetric groups, and current status.
Jensen, Ledet and Yui, Generic Polynomials: Constructive Aspects of the Inverse Galois Problem (2002), Introduction §§0.1–0.2, pp. 1–4: https://library.slmath.org/books/Book45/files/book45start.pdf
https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~matyd/InvGal/ — PCMI 2021 inverse Galois course introduction, research discussion, and recommended reading.

Local Mathlib sources: FieldTheory/Galois/Basic.lean; FieldTheory/Normal/Defs.lean; FieldTheory/Separable.lean; FieldTheory/IsAlgClosed/Basic.lean; FieldTheory/RatFunc/{Defs,Basic}.lean; Algebra/Algebra/{Defs,Equiv}.lean; Algebra/Group/{Defs,End}.lean; Algebra/CharZero/Defs.lean; GroupTheory/SpecificGroups/Cyclic/Basic.lean; Data/Fintype/Defs.lean.
review.notes: Checked both definitions and all six theorems. The main problem remains open in the current cited source; the cyclic, abelian, symmetric, and complex rational-function variants have the recorded solved status. No independent stale-status issue was found. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and verifies the realization equivalence, invariance under group isomorphism, realizations of trivial groups (including permutations of empty and singleton sets), and CharZero ℚ together with ¬ IsAlgClosed ℚ. The equivalence and boundary proofs use no sorry axioms.

not_demonstrated.reason: The missing algebraic-closedness hypothesis produces a stronger, unresolved assertion, not a known false or trivially true statement. Its specialization to K = ℚ asserts realizability of every finite group over ℚ(t), which would imply the inverse Galois conjecture over ℚ by Hilbert irreducibility. Showing CharZero ℚ and ¬ IsAlgClosed ℚ confirms the enlarged domain but does not prove or refute the declaration.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created, and no compilation was attempted. The source mismatch remains substantiated, but it does not yield a short proof or disproof of the formalized theorem.
submission.gave_up_reason: No short, honest proof or disproof of the reported overgeneralization is available; the truth of the stronger assertion is unresolved. Applying the repository's sorry-backed theorem would not constitute a demonstration.

submission.summary: Added the missing [IsAlgClosed K] hypothesis and updated the docstring to require an algebraically closed coefficient field of characteristic zero. All other declarations and attributes are unchanged. The edited file compiles with only the expected 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
